A.explanation: Forces are opposite but separation is only $d$, so couple torque is $F \times d = Fd$, smaller than the maximum.

B.explanation: Both forces act upward in the same direction, so they give a resultant force $2F$ but no couple and no free torque.

C.explanation: Both forces act upward in the same direction with separation $2d$, so they do not form an opposite couple and produce no pure torque.

D.explanation: Forces are opposite with perpendicular separation $2d$, so couple torque is $F \times 2d = 2Fd$, the largest.

hints: Notice whether the two $F$ arrows in each diagram point in opposite directions or in the same upward direction.
Recall that only opposite parallel forces form a couple with free torque $torque = F \times separation$.
Compare the perpendicular separation between the lines of action: $d$ in A and $2d$ in D for the opposite pairs.
walkthrough: Identify the rod length $5d$ and two forces each of magnitude $F$ applied perpendicular to the rod.
State the rule: largest turning effect comes from an opposite pair forming a couple, with $torque = F \times$ perpendicular separation between the forces.
Check directions: A and D have opposite forces, B and C have both forces upward so they give resultant force, not a couple.
Compare separations of the opposite pairs: A has separation $d$ giving $F \times d = Fd$.
D has separation $2d$ giving $F \times 2d = 2Fd$, which is greater than A and greater than the zero couple in B and C.
